description: Tell the digits apart with a support vector machine (RBF)
content: An SVM with an RBF kernel. Use scikit-learn's SVC. C (default 5.0) and gamma (default 0.02) are parameters. Add to the figure the number of support vectors per digit next to the number of training images. data is the path of prepare's npz file: train_images and test_images are 784-dimensional arrays scaled to 0–1, train_labels and test_labels are digits, digest is a fingerprint of the test images. Set OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 at the top of main.py (before the imports) to run on one thread. Measure training and prediction times as differences of time.process_time(). The type of the output result is the same for all seven classifiers, and compare reads it with one type, so _outputs.fbs is, without changing a character, "namespace mnist; table Result { model:string; settings:string; digest:string; accuracy:double; fit_seconds:double; predict_seconds:double; predictions:[ubyte] (required); } table Outputs { result:Result (required); } root_type Outputs;". model is the Card's id, settings a string of the parameters' values, digest the value received as it is, and predictions the predictions for every test image. Show the accuracy, the times and a breakdown of the mistakes (a 10×10 table of true and predicted) in a matplotlib figure. Assert: that the length of predictions equals the number of test images, that every prediction is 0–9, that the accuracy is at least 0.95, that the total number of support vectors is at least 1 and at most the number of training images, and that the sum of n_support_ equals the length of support_, and that the accuracy on the training images is at least that on the test images. Use numpy, matplotlib and scikit-learn.
